name: Gehazi
charge: Running after Naaman to take what his master refused; lying to Naaman and then to the prophet’s face
summary: When Elisha refused Naaman’s gifts, his servant Gehazi ran after the Syrian’s chariot, invented a message from his master asking silver and clothing for two young prophets, and hid the two talents and the garments in the house (2 Kings 5:20-24). He lied again to Elisha’s face, and Elisha told him his heart had gone with him; Naaman’s leprosy would cling to him and his descendants for ever, and he went out a leper white as snow (2 Kings 5:25-27).
offenseFull: Elisha had refused Naaman’s gifts, swearing by the Lord before whom he stood (2 Kings 5:16). Gehazi, his servant, told himself his master had let this Syrian off too lightly, and swore by the Lord to run after him and get something from him (2 Kings 5:20). He had been Elisha’s understudy and seen all the miracles, and he was still looking at all that glitter. When Naaman saw him running he got down from his chariot and asked whether all was well. Gehazi said it was, and that his master had sent him to ask a talent of silver and two changes of clothing for two young men of the sons of the prophets just arrived from the hill country of Ephraim (2 Kings 5:21-22). Naaman told him to be content and take two talents, and pressed them on him; Gehazi should have woken up then (2 Kings 5:23). At the hill he took the bags from Naaman’s servants, hid them in the house like a thief, and sent the men away (2 Kings 5:24).

Then he went in and stood before his master, and when Elisha asked where he had been, he said he had gone nowhere (2 Kings 5:25). Covetousness makes a man lie, and Gehazi lied twice, adding sin to sin, because he would not control it. The study notes say it shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks, hasty to grasp things by unjust means. Elisha had asked Elijah for a double portion of his spirit, not for money and clothes. The real men of God do not do the Lord’s work for a reward; they trust Him to provide.
judgmentFull: Elisha asked whether his heart had not gone with him when the man turned from his chariot to meet him (2 Kings 5:26). God sees it all; the spirit of the Lord reveals what is done in secret, so do not lie before righteous men, but come correct. He asked whether this was a time to take money and clothes, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen, and servants (2 Kings 5:26). There is a season for everything, a time to get and a time to lose (Ecclesiastes 3:1, 6), and Elisha explained that there was a time to receive, and this was not it.

The leprosy of Naaman would cling to Gehazi and to his descendants for ever, and he went out from Elisha’s presence a leper, white as snow (2 Kings 5:27). The same sickness that had just left Naaman came on him. He was judged immediately. Many think they are fine because judgment is slow, but the money they love will destroy them. The work of one sinner cost his whole lineage: he destroyed not only himself

but his children. The teaching applies it to generational curses, telling the hearers to examine whether they are paying for the sins of their parents. The class on generational curses reads the leprosy white as snow as the whole skin with its pigment gone, which the law calls the clean leprosy when it covers the body from head to foot (Leviticus 13:12-13). It teaches that this is how Cain was cursed from the ground and how Esau was born, and that the look of white people is that curse. Because it was laid on his seed for ever, the class teaches that Gehazi’s descendants are here today and carry it. The remedy the law gives for a generational curse is to confess the iniquity of the fathers and accept its punishment, and then the Lord remembers His covenant (Leviticus 26:40-42).

text.text: But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, Behold, my master hath spared Naaman this Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought: but, as the Lord liveth, I will run after him, and take somewhat of him.
So Gehazi followed after Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running after him, he lighted down from the chariot to meet him, and said, Is all well?

And he said, All is well. My master hath sent me, saying, Behold, even now there be come to me from mount Ephraim two young men of the sons of the prophets: give them, I pray thee, a talent of silver, and two changes of garments.

And Naaman said, Be content, take two talents. And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and laid them upon two of his servants; and they bare them before him.
And when he came to the tower, he took them from their hand, and bestowed them in the house: and he let the men go, and they departed.
But he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said unto him, Whence comest thou, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went no whither.

And he said unto him, Went not mine heart with thee, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?
The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow.
But he said, As the Lord liveth, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take it; but he refused.

To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow.
And if a leprosy break out abroad in the skin, and the leprosy cover all the skin of him that hath the plague from his head even to his foot, wheresoever the priest looketh;
Then the priest shall consider: and, behold, if the leprosy have covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean that hath the plague: it is all turned white: he is clean.
If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me;

And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity:
Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.

And when he came to the tower, he took them from their hand, and bestowed them in the house: and he let the men go, and they departed.
But he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said unto him, Whence comest thou, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went no whither.
For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
